entries.effect: the accessors are the port's own: a fresh task has no delegate of its own although its session has one, a delegate set on the task reads back, and it is refused after the task resumes with the system's own NSGenericException and reason. revenant_task_delegate() in NSURLSession.m is the one place that decides, and it decides PER SELECTOR as the header says: a method the task's own delegate does not implement still goes to the session's delegate, so all seventeen task-scoped guards and sends read the delegate that answers the selector being sent. Once the task has completed the delegate reads nil

entries.source: the accessors, sh tests/backports/host/attributed15/run.sh in the four cases task.freshDelegate, task.freshDelegate.port, task.setAndReadBack and task.systemReadBack. The three rules the header states beside the property, measured on the system's own NSURLSession by sh tests/backports/host/tasksession/run.sh on macOS 27.0 build 26A428 arm64, 10 checks and 0 failures with its control run first: a delegate implementing nothing left the session delegate hearing URLSession:task:didCompleteWithError: once and a delegate implementing exactly that selector heard it once with the session delegate hearing zero, which is the per-selector answer; -setDelegate: after -resume raised NSGenericException with the reason 'Cannot set task delegate after resumption'; and -delegate read nil once the completion had been delivered. The port's own routing cannot be measured here, because the port's NSURLSession is a class the host also defines and that file cannot be linked beside the host's - tests/backports/device/ios1516.m is where it runs, and this band did not run it
